reasons: Both answers correct the accountant, explain the IP filing duty and the ITSGF above 3M EUR, cover Modelo 720, the Beckham regime and overdue deadlines, and recommend a Spanish adviser, so every rubric item is met by both. B is slightly more thorough on residence-year timing and valuation, but it gets the joint 60% cap backwards: low taxable income from an ETF portfolio makes the cap more likely to cut the bill, not less. A describes the cap correctly and points out the practical mitigation, which gives it a small edge.

A: Suggests quoted securities are valued at the Q4 average price for IP; ETFs as collective investment vehicles are generally valued at year-end liquidation or market value (minor)
B: Claims the IRPF+IP/ITSGF 60% cap usually does not help much when the ETF portfolio produces modest income; low taxable income is exactly when the cap binds and can cut the wealth taxes by up to 80%
